title: Smooth weakly modular graphs
summary: A graph $G=(V,E)$ is called smooth (respectively, strongly smooth) if for any two vertices $u,v\in V$, the distance point-shadow $v|u := \{ x\in V: d(u,x)=d(u,v)+d(v,x)\}$, respectively, the point-shadow $v/u := \{ x\in V: v\in\mathrm{conv}(u,x)\}$, is geodesically convex. Smooth graphs have been introduced by Nebeský (2005) in the context of step systems. Graphs with convex point-shadows and convex distance point-shadows also naturally occur in convexity theory.
